description: Deterministic release-gate contract for the PetTripFinder Columbus market (PETTRIPFINDER-PROD-005A, re-scoped per market by PTF-PER-MARKET-RELEASE-CONTRACTS-001). Consumed by scripts/pettripfinder/assemble_netlify_bundle.py. Complete and self-contained: it inherits nothing from another market, and no other market may be assembled against it. Contains NO credentials and NO remote project identifiers. The committed hotel-policy package is the single identity authority for the verified hotels; this contract deliberately does NOT duplicate a hard-coded production allow-list.

deployment_authorization.means: A passing contract means this market's assembled package is STRUCTURALLY deployable: its authority files agree, its routes match its reviewed inventory, no held identity leaks, and every publish/tech gate holds. It is not a deployment authorization and it makes no claim that the market's identity universe is fully resolved.

identity_census.note: Created by PTF-CENSUS-PARTITION-NORMALIZATION-001. Columbus had no committed census: its universe of 112 lived only in a work-order report, so this contract could state neither a confirmed count nor an unresolved one. The census reconstructs those 112 identities from committed authority alone -- 89 seed inventory rows this market owns, 16 exclusion registry rows, and 7 routing records for identities in neither, three sets that do not overlap -- and every row records which of them it came from.

identity_census_note: Columbus commits no identity-census file: its confirmed universe was established in work-order reports, not in a versioned census document. The reconciliation below therefore states confirmed_identities and unresolved as null. Absent is a fact; zero would be a claim, and a gate would happily compare against it.

reconciliation.note: verified_no_pets counts ONLY VERIFIED_NO_PETS records this market owns in launch_packages/pettripfinder/hotel_exclusions.json. The registry also holds two OUT_OF_CURRENT_CATEGORY rows for Columbus, which are a category ruling and not negative pet evidence. unresolved is now COUNTED from columbus_final_partition_001.json rather than derived by subtraction. The difference is not cosmetic: subtracting published and no-pets from the universe gave 10, because it treated the two OUT_OF_CURRENT_CATEGORY rows as unresolved when they are a category ruling. The eight are one held seed row awaiting a policy artifact, six routed identities awaiting a policy observation, and one awaiting routing review. resolved counts all three TERMINAL dispositions -- published, verified no-pets, and the two category exits -- because a category ruling settles an identity just as finally as a refusal does.

policy_package.note: The verified hotel identities are DERIVED from this package at assembly time via scripts.pettripfinder.site_data.verified_public_hotels(); they are not restated here. Held/manual-review hotels are this market's seed hotels absent from this package.

public_surface.held_hotel_exclusion: Every seed hotel this market owns that is absent from the committed package (not-published seed hotels: held/manual-review plus rows still pending evidence) must have NO public route and NO reference on any surface: hotel profiles, the hotels listing/category page, nearby-lodging cards on any page, the policy-comparison table, the sitemap, canonicals, internal links, and /go/ interstitials.

routes.note: route_mode legacy_unprefixed keeps Columbus's live unprefixed routes (/pet-friendly-hotels/{hotel_slug}/) until its URL migration is explicitly approved; see launch_packages/pettripfinder/markets/reports/columbus-oh_route_migration.md.

publish.note: The publish root must contain ONLY the static website plus the two Netlify control files. Build-internal reports the generator emits (_build_report.json, _broken_link_report.json, _quality_report.json, bundle_manifest.json) are read for gating but are excluded from site/ and must never ship.
